solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Decay beginning to show in hideous couple

indicators.note: the opening letter is placed inside the word for hideous

parts.note: hideous means dire, dreadful

indicators.note: the start of the word show supplies just its first letter

parts.note: a couple is a pair

explanation.surface: Something ugly and paired starts to reveal rot, like a crumbling old house.
explanation.definitionFit: A building in bad repair has fallen into decay; the noun names that neglected, ruined state.

clue.text: Detective Inspector Morse ultimately tough on southern reactionaries

parts.note: DI is the police abbreviation for Detective Inspector

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the name Morse

parts.note: tough means hard

explanation.surface: Inspector Morse, the TV detective, finally takes a hard line on reactionary southerners.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspector Morse is a British TV detective, which makes 'Detective Inspector Morse' read as one name; it splits into DI and the last letter of Morse.
explanation.definitionFit: Die-hards are stubborn resisters of change, so the word is a near-synonym for conservative reactionaries.

clue.text: Disgraceful mark time erased in letter to Greeks

indicators.note: erased means the letter for time is wiped out of the longer word

parts.note: a stigma is a mark of disgrace

explanation.surface: A shameful blot on the record is wiped away in a letter sent to the Greeks.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the eighteenth character of the Greek alphabet, so it is literally a letter belonging to Greeks.

clue.text: Course incomplete with reason given in confidence

indicators.note: incomplete means the word for a course loses its final letter

parts.note: an entree is a course of a meal
nous is common sense, reason

explanation.surface: A half-finished course is supplied with a justification, all told privately.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase meaning between ourselves is used in English for something said privately, in confidence.

clue.text: Embarrassed because news boss engages amateur

indicators.note: engages here means the editor takes on the amateur, who stands in front of the boss's abbreviation

parts.note: as can mean because
a ham is an amateur, as in a ham radio operator or poor actor
ED, short for editor, is the boss of a newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone is red-faced since their newspaper editor has hired a novice.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling shame or awkwardness is the same as being embarrassed; the words are close synonyms.

clue.text: Little man with money recited poem

indicators.note: recited means the phrase is spoken, and its sound gives the letters

parts.note: Ron, a short form of Ronald, is the little man, and dough is slang for money

explanation.surface: A small fellow with cash reads out a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondeau is a French verse form of thirteen or so lines on two rhymes with a refrain, so a kind of poem.

clue.text: Cheat cold seeping into unfinished dwelling

indicators.note: seeping into means the abbreviation for cold goes inside the shortened dwelling
unfinished means the word for a dwelling loses its last letter

parts.note: a house is a dwelling
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A chill creeps into a half-built home, like a con that leaves a house unfinished.
explanation.definitionFit: To hocus, as in hocus-pocus, is an old verb meaning to trick or swindle someone.

clue.text: Leader abandons modest expedition

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter, which is dropped from the word for modest

parts.note: chaste means modest, pure

explanation.surface: The head of a small, unassuming journey walks out on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expedition' looks like a journey, but here it has its older sense of speed, as in 'with all expedition'.
explanation.definitionFit: Expedition can mean promptness or speed of action, a sense matching rush or hurry.

clue.text: One to blend in drink with energy-packed fruit

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea, a drink

indicators.note: packed means the letter for energy is stuffed into the fruit

parts.note: a melon is a fruit
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Something to mix into a drink alongside an energy-rich fruit, like a smoothie recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blend in' suggests mixing a drink, but it means merging with the background.
explanation.definitionFit: This lizard changes colour to match its surroundings, so it is the classic creature that blends in.

clue.text: Small study about headless sheep in northern kingdom

indicators.note: about means the small-plus-study pieces go around the shortened sheep

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes
a den is a study, a private room for work

indicators.note: headless means the word for sheep loses its first letter

parts.note: a ewe is a female sheep

explanation.surface: A little paper on a sheep lacking a head, written somewhere in the far north.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a Scandinavian monarchy in northern Europe, so a northern kingdom.

clue.text: Figure of one stone, perhaps, with front obscured

indicators.note: the front letter of the weight word is hidden from view and removed

parts.note: one stone is an example of a weight, the stone being a British unit of 14 pounds

explanation.surface: A shape of a single rock is partly hidden at its front.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British unit of weight equal to 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a number, and figure is a common word for a numeral.

clue.text: Greeting crew members with fish

parts.note: hands are crew members on a ship
hake is a fish

explanation.surface: Sailors meet each other bearing a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Clasping and shaking another's palm is a customary greeting on meeting someone.

clue.text: An aspiration to entertain ambassador in Californian city

indicators.note: to entertain means the aim word plays host to the ambassador's letters

parts.note: an aim is an aspiration
HE, His Excellency, is the form of address for an ambassador

explanation.surface: Someone hopes to host a diplomat in a city in California.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a city in Orange County, southern California, home of Disneyland.

clue.text: Interpreter for example appearing in late summer in France

indicators.note: appearing in means the example abbreviation shows up inside the other pieces

parts.note: ex means former, late, as in an ex-wife
ete is French for summer

explanation.surface: A translator for example shows up in France at the end of summer.
explanation.definitionFit: An exegete explains and interprets texts, especially scripture.

clue.text: Rock festival featuring Queen?

parts.note: a diamond is a rock, slang for a gem
a jubilee is a festival or celebration

explanation.surface: A rock music festival with the band Queen on the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen looks like the rock band, but the whole clue describes Elizabeth II's 60th-anniversary celebration in 2012.
explanation.definitionFit: This sixtieth-anniversary celebration of a reign was a festival centred on the monarch herself.

clue.text: Brute concealing old record is to put things straight

indicators.note: concealing means the primate word hides the other pieces inside it

parts.note: an ape is a brute
a log is a record

explanation.surface: A beast hides an old vinyl disc, and must make amends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record' suggests a vinyl disc, but it is a log, a written record.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying sorry is how one sets matters right after a wrong, so it puts things straight.

clue.text: Hint Tunisian criminal gave at last

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters of Tunisian are corrupted into a new order
at last means just the final letter of gave is taken

explanation.surface: A North African wrongdoer finally gave a clue to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: To insinuate is to suggest something indirectly, a near-synonym for the verb hint.

clue.text: Boring race gives no decisive result

parts.note: dead can mean boring, lifeless, as in a dead party
a heat is a race

explanation.surface: A dull race ends without a clear winner.
explanation.definitionFit: When runners cross the line together nobody wins outright, giving no decisive result.

clue.text: Complaint in sheikdom — unease to spread

indicators.note: to spread means the letters of the two words are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A malaise in a sheikdom is causing unrest to spread.
explanation.definitionFit: This inflammation of the knee from kneeling to scrub floors is a medical complaint, or ailment.

clue.text: Carriage cutting horse in two — it's gruesome

indicators.note: cutting means the carriage word slices into the horse word
in two says the horse word is split into two halves around the carriage

parts.note: a mare is a female horse
a cab is a carriage, originally horse-drawn

explanation.surface: A coach chopping a horse in half is a grisly sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dealing with death in a horrifying way is grisly, the sense of the adjective here.

clue.text: Understanding current things differently

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

indicators.note: differently means the letters of things are arranged in another way

explanation.surface: Seeing present-day matters in a new way brings understanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Insight is a deep grasp or perception of something, a synonym for understanding.

clue.text: Eating too much, mole covered in pimples

indicators.note: eating means the mole word swallows the excess abbreviation

parts.note: a mole is a spy who works inside an organisation
OTT, over the top, means too much

explanation.surface: A mole that overeats ends up covered in spots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mole' suggests a skin blemish, matching the pimples, but it is the undercover agent.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone covered in pimples has a spotty complexion; the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Expert thus securing a flat

parts.note: a pro is an expert

indicators.note: securing means the word for thus holds the a inside it

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus, used to mark a quotation as printed

explanation.surface: A professional thereby gets hold of an apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like an apartment, but it is the adjective meaning dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat in the sense of dull and unimaginative is close to commonplace, matter-of-fact writing.

clue.text: Up to each person

parts.note: a means each, as in five pounds a time
head means a person, as in ten pounds per head

explanation.surface: It is the individual's choice.
explanation.definitionFit: A team that is up by two goals is leading, in front of the other side.

clue.text: Flighty African needs daily porridge

parts.note: the Sun is a British daily newspaper
porridge and bird are both British slang for a prison sentence

explanation.surface: A capricious African insists on eating porridge every day.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British daily tabloid, and 'porridge' and 'bird' are both British slang for time in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: This small nectar-feeding bird lives in Africa, and 'flighty' playfully says it flies.

clue.text: Lemur visible in thin drizzle

indicators.note: visible in means the letters can be seen inside the phrase thin drizzle

explanation.surface: A lemur can be glimpsed through light rain.
explanation.definitionFit: The indri is the largest living lemur, native to Madagascar.

clue.text: One allowed carrier in kit: something for soap etc

indicators.note: in means the other pieces sit inside the word for kit

parts.note: tog, as in togs, means clothes or kit
I is the Roman numeral for one
let means allowed
BA, British Airways, is an airline, a carrier

explanation.surface: A person may take a bag in their luggage, holding soap and the like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrier' suggests a bag, but it is the airline British Airways.
explanation.definitionFit: A wash bag is a small case for holding soap, toothbrush and other toiletries when travelling.

clue.text: Confuse theologian introduced to beer

indicators.note: introduced to means the theologian's letters are put into the beer

parts.note: ale is beer
DD, Doctor of Divinity, denotes a theologian

explanation.surface: A divine is given beer and gets befuddled.
explanation.definitionFit: To addle is to muddle or befuddle someone's mind, so it means confuse.

clue.text: Yankee, ridiculously idle, has to give up

parts.note: Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: ridiculously means the letters of idle are put into an absurd new order

explanation.surface: An American, foolishly lazy, has to throw in the towel.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield is to surrender or concede, a synonym for give up.

clue.text: Fanatic to survive bracing term at sea

indicators.note: bracing means the survive word holds the jumbled letters within it, like a brace

parts.note: exist means to survive

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of term are muddled

explanation.surface: A zealot hopes to get through an invigorating spell on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bracing' suggests sea air but means holding; 'at sea' gives TREM, the anagram of TERM, inside EXIST.
explanation.definitionFit: An extremist holds radical views, and a fanatic is one such zealous person.
